page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a burstable, shared-core virtual machine belonging to the e2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs allocated from a 1/8 shared physical core, supporting hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. It includes 1.0 GB of system memory, providing 0.5 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware included with this instance type, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the e2-micro in the lower tier of performance, consistently scoring in the bottom 10% across multiple tests. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is rated at 132.9, while multi-core performance reaches 171.0. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, with read-only small block cached speeds at 9.73 GB/sec, dropping to 0.1 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and write speeds at 1.33 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 201.56 and 176.45 respectively. Redis SET operations achieve 0.2 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is limited to 0.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-micro offers a low-resource, budget-friendly profile designed for minimal workloads where continuous high-performance CPU allocation is unnecessary. Given the shared-core CPU architecture and 1.0 GB memory limit, this instance is suited for lightweight utility tasks, basic testing, low-traffic static web serving, or small background scripts rather than database hosting or memory-intensive applications.
